intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that atrial standstill-1 (ATRST1) is caused by mutation in the SCN5A gene (600163) on chromosome 3p22.2, in combination with rare polymorphisms in the GJA5 gene (121013) on chromosome 1q21.2.

checks.claim: Atrial standstill-1 (ATRST1) is caused by mutation in the SCN5A gene in combination with rare polymorphisms in the GJA5 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: In this study, familial AS was associated with the concurrence of a cardiac sodium channel mutation and rare polymorphisms in the atrial-specific Cx40 gene.
checks.explanation: The paper reports an association and a proposed combined effect; the draft's statement that it is 'caused' is stronger than the abstract.

checks.explanation: The chromosomal location is standard nomenclature; GJA5 is the approved symbol for Cx40.

paragraphs.text: Atrial standstill is a rare arrhythmia that occasionally appears to be genetically determined (Groenewegen et al., 2003). Fazelifar et al. (2005) described it as an extremely uncommon arrhythmia that is rarely familial. They noted that it has been associated with several conditions, including congenital heart disease, valvular heart disease, conduction disturbances, Brugada syndrome, myocardial infarction, and amyloidosis.

paragraphs.text: Groenewegen et al. (2003) found that, in a large family with atrial standstill, the affected members had coinherited an SCN5A mutation and a rare homozygous GJA5 (connexin-40) genotype. Unaffected relatives carried the SCN5A mutation alone or the GJA5 genotype alone. The authors proposed that the combined effect of these genetic changes eventually progresses to total atrial standstill, which suggests digenic inheritance.

paragraphs.text: Groenewegen et al. (2003) screened candidate genes in a large family with atrial standstill. They identified a novel asp1275-to-asn (D1275N) mutation in the SCN5A gene in all 3 affected living relatives and in 5 unaffected relatives; the deceased affected relative was an obligate carrier. They also found 2 closely linked polymorphisms in regulatory regions of the gene for the atrial-specific gap junction protein connexin-40 (GJA5), at nucleotides -44 (G-A) and +71 (A-G). Eight relatives were homozygous for both polymorphisms, and 3 of these were affected. The 3 living patients were the only relatives who had coinherited both the rare connexin-40 genotype and the SCN5A D1275N mutation. In functional studies, D1275N channels showed a small depolarizing shift in activation compared with wildtype channels. In reporter gene analysis, the rare connexin-40 genotype reduced expression compared with the more common genotype. Homozygosity for both polymorphisms occurred in only about 7% of control subjects. The authors proposed that the functional effect of each genetic change alone is relatively benign, but that their combined effect eventually progresses to total atrial standstill.

paragraphs.text: Makita et al. (2005) screened SCN5A and atrial-specific genes, including GJA5 (connexin-40), in the family of an 11-year-old boy with atrial standstill. They identified a novel leu212-to-pro (L212P) mutation in SCN5A in the proband and in his father, who was in normal sinus rhythm. In whole-cell patch-clamp studies, the recombinant L212P sodium channel showed a large hyperpolarizing shift in the voltage dependence of activation (wildtype, -48.1 +/- 0.9 mV; L212P, -63.5 +/- 1.5 mV) and of inactivation (wildtype, -86.6 +/- 0.9 mV; L212P, -95.6 +/- 0.8 mV). It also showed delayed recovery from inactivation. The proband, but not his father, also carried connexin-40 polymorphisms inherited from his asymptomatic mother.
